Container.Name: dify-aio
Container.Overview:
Dify is a self-hosted AI application platform for agentic workflows, RAG pipelines, tools, model-provider integrations, and observability.
[b]All-In-One Unraid Edition[/b] `dify-aio` packages the Dify API, workers, web UI, plugin daemon, code sandbox, SSRF proxy, Nginx, PostgreSQL with pgvector, and Redis into one practical Unraid-first container.
[b]Quick Install (Beginners)[/b] 1. Install this template and leave [code]Web UI Port[/code] and [code]AppData[/code] at their defaults unless you already have a port conflict. 2. Start the container and give first boot a few minutes. The wrapper initializes bundled PostgreSQL, pgvector, Redis, generated secrets, local storage, the sandbox, plugin daemon, and the Dify services. 3. Open the Web UI and create the first admin account. You can optionally set [code]Initial Admin Password[/code] before first boot, but it is not required. 4. Add model-provider credentials inside Dify first. For a reverse proxy or published apps, set [code]Public URL[/code] to your external HTTPS URL and restart. 5. Keep Advanced View defaults for the easiest install. The bundled database, cache, vector store, local file storage, sandbox, and SSRF proxy are already wired together.
[b]Power Users (Advanced View)[/b] - Advanced View exposes external PostgreSQL-compatible databases, Redis, object storage, vector databases, SMTP/mail, plugin storage, observability, CORS/CSP, sandbox, proxy, token expiry, indexing, cleanup, and broader upstream Dify environment controls. - If you switch a backend selector such as [code]VECTOR_STORE[/code], [code]STORAGE_TYPE[/code], [code]DB_TYPE[/code], or internal service toggles, configure the matching companion fields for that backend. - Blank secret fields generate and persist values in [code]/appdata/config/generated.env[/code]. Explicit Unraid template values override generated secrets, and [code]/appdata/config/extra.env[/code] remains the final advanced override escape hatch. - [code]CHECK_UPDATE_URL[/code] is blank by default to avoid outbound update checks unless you intentionally opt in.
[b]Important Notes[/b] - Dify is a heavier multi-service stack. Plan for at least 2 CPU cores and 4 GiB RAM, with more memory for real indexing, workflow, or model-heavy workloads. - Public exposure should sit behind a trusted reverse proxy with TLS. Review sandbox/network settings before allowing untrusted users to run code or tools. - External vector stores, object storage, SMTP, and model providers are optional but real production deployments may need them.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Dify Web UI and API gateway port.

Config.Name: AppData
Config.Description: Persistent Dify data, generated secrets, PostgreSQL data, Redis data, uploads, plugin storage, and sandbox configuration.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: Optional external base URL such as https://dify.example.com. Used to default Dify console, app, trigger, WebSocket, and file URLs.

Config.Name: Initial Admin Password
Config.Description: Optional initial admin password. Dify limits this value to 30 characters. Leave blank to set the admin account during first-run setup.

Config.Name: Deploy Environment
Config.Description: Dify deployment environment mode. Keep PRODUCTION for normal Unraid installs.

Config.Name: Dify Update Check URL
Config.Description: Optional Dify update-check endpoint. Leave blank to disable outbound update checks for privacy-focused or offline installs.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Dify application secret key. Leave blank to generate and persist one on first boot. Changing this after setup invalidates encrypted credentials and sessions.

Config.Name: Use Internal PostgreSQL
Config.Description: Use the bundled PostgreSQL 15 database with pgvector. Set false only when using an external PostgreSQL-compatible database.

Config.Name: Database Type
Config.Description: Database type used by Dify. The bundled AIO database is PostgreSQL; non-PostgreSQL modes require external infrastructure.

Config.Name: Database Host
Config.Description: PostgreSQL host. Keep 127.0.0.1 for bundled PostgreSQL.

Config.Name: Database Password
Config.Description: PostgreSQL password. Leave blank to generate and persist one on first boot.

Config.Name: Database Name
Config.Description: PostgreSQL database used by the Dify API.

Config.Name: Plugin Database Name
Config.Description: PostgreSQL database used by the Dify plugin daemon.

Config.Name: Use Internal Redis
Config.Description: Use the bundled Redis instance. Set false only when using an external Redis service.

Config.Name: Redis Host
Config.Description: Redis host. Keep 127.0.0.1 for bundled Redis.

Config.Name: Redis Password
Config.Description: Redis password. Leave blank to generate and persist one on first boot.

Config.Name: Celery Broker URL
Config.Description: Optional explicit Celery broker URL. Leave blank to derive it from Redis settings.

Config.Name: Console API URL
Config.Description: Optional public console API URL. Leave blank to derive from Public URL or incoming requests.

Config.Name: Console Web URL
Config.Description: Optional public console web URL. Leave blank to derive from Public URL or incoming requests.

Config.Name: Service API URL
Config.Description: Optional public Service API URL shown inside Dify. Leave blank to derive from Public URL or incoming requests.

Config.Name: Trigger URL
Config.Description: Optional public trigger URL. Leave blank to derive from Public URL or use Dify defaults.

Config.Name: App API URL
